Problems for passive Man City as Chelsea are bullied by Leeds - Premier League hits and misses
Sky Sports' football writers analyse Saturday's Premier League action as Man City are held by Fulham, Leeds rip Chelsea apart, Luca Williams-Barnett stars for Spurs, Bournemouth win again, and Coventry make it a losing start for Thomas Frank with Crystal Palace
Saturday 21 November 2026 20:09, UK
Man City far too passive against Fulham
Enzo Maresca had insisted after the defeat to Nottingham Forest that there was no overarching theme to their losing run. But the results are a recurring problem. They at least mustered a draw at home to Fulham but the performance was not convincing.
Against Forest, Maresca highlighted lost duels as an issue, most conspicuously for Liam Delap's first goal when Elliot Anderson came out second best against Xaver Schlager. His team selection hinted at an attempt to address that with Ayyoub Bouaddi included.
But City still looked too easy to play through. Fulham managed it time and time again. Perhaps it is the lack of pressing from the front that is part of the problem, as much as a lack of defensive cover in midfield. Erling Haaland certainly seemed reluctant to do so.

The fans were groaning in frustration at how comfortable Fulham looked right from the start and their tolerance for what might be deemed a passive possession game is declining. Maresca's controlled approach is not bringing the control that he needs.
Adam Bate
Fulham end losing streak against Man City
Nobody gets the better of Fulham 18 times in a row. Their run of 17 Premier League defeats to Man City finally came to an end and they deserved their 1-1 draw. Alvaro Arbeloa's commitment to a possession game is impressive and starting to get its rewards.
The Spaniard was under pressure after an unconvincing start that contrasted with Enzo Maresca's seven-game winning streak to start the campaign. But while their teams could not be separated, it is Arbeloa's Fulham's looking more confident and purposeful.
They played through press, not easy to do even if City did look a little disjointed, and defended bravely. Calvin Bassey was prepared to follow Phil Foden deep into opposition territory. David Affengruber was trusted to face Erling Haaland one-against-one.
It was bold, and had Fulham been punished it would have been easy to say - and indeed write - that it was expecting too much of his team. But the Fulham players' belief in this style of play is growing. They are five unbeaten after that shaky start. Promising form.
Adam Bate
Leeds follow familiar blueprint to beat Chelsea
There is a blueprint to beat Xabi Alonso's Chelsea that Sunderland, Tottenham, Brentford, and now Leeds have all exposed: run hard, win duels, and press the defence.
In all those defeats, Chelsea have been outrun and although Alonso says he looks to find "football solutions" to their problems, there is no denying that his side has a physicality issue.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats
Once Moises Caicedo went off injured against Leeds, Chelsea were completely overpowered. Dominic Calvert-Lewin schooled Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill with his forward play, Ethan Ampadu edged Jordan Henderson closer to retirement and Estevao and Cole Palmer were bullied. "They couldn't handle it," said Calvert-Lewin.
As tension rose at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea couldn't find a way through Leeds' press to their forwards, creating an attacking issue too. Chelsea created just 0.58 xG and zero big chances compared to Leeds' seven.
Alonso is now under pressure after three defeats in four league games and admitted his side are "fragile" heading to Nottingham Forest next Friday. They need to toughen up fast.
David Richardson
Teenager Williams-Barnett shines on first Spurs start
What a memorable full debut for Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett.
After a handful of encouraging substitute displays this season, the 18-year-old was deservedly handed his first Spurs start - and boy did he take it to inspire Spurs to a 2-0 home win over Ipswich.
He dazzled on the left wing and scored the opener to become the youngest Spurs player to score on his first Premier League start for the club. He also became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).
Bale would go on to become a Spurs great, and there will be optimism that Williams-Barnett can do the same.
Every time he touched the ball in the win over Ipswich, there was real excitement at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has been in short supply in recent times.
He was a constant threat to the Ipswich defence as defenders backed off him, which exactly led to Solanke's goal.
The stats back up his impressive performance - he had the most touches in the opposition box (8) and big chances (2) of any player, while no player had more than his four shots on target.
For all of Spurs' big summer spending, their new hero looks to be from within.
Declan Olley
Villa signed a lot of replacements - but not one for Tielemans
Aston Villa made a lot of signings to replace the players they lost in the summer. Nicolas Jackson came in for Ollie Watkins. Johan Manzambi arrived to fill the void Morgan Rogers left.
Matteo Ruggeri, when fit, has looked promising after Lucas Digne left. Zion Suzuki has been a strong heir to Emiliano Martinez's throne. The list goes on.
But they did not replace Youri Tielemans. His composure on the ball, paired with his eye and ability to find the killer pass to unlock defences, has been missing all season but his absence is felt most in games like this.
Sunderland sat deep, denied Villa space and absorbed the pressure. They asked Unai Emery's side to come at them, which they did, and dealt with it all.
Leon Goretzka is more of a stopper in midfield. Joao Gomes gets forward in flashes but is more all-action in his approach.
Tielemans was the man capable of carving out opportunities in games like this. They are now missing that profile, the Adam Wharton template style player, that helps them when all other avenues are shut off.
Patrick Rowe
Ancelotti, are you watching? Evanilson spearheading Bournemouth form
Evanilson is the attacking heart of Bournemouth's club-record nine wins in a row. The Cherries have averaged 2.56 goals per game on that run and the Brazilian has been at the centre of it all.
His brilliantly-executed opener in the 18th minute against Nottingham Forest was already his third shot on target. There was almost a telepathic understanding between Evanilson and his team-mates of the spaces in which he could pick up dangerous balls.
In the second half, he turned more of a provider, especially trying to tee up fellow Brazilian Rayan for a Bournemouth third that ultimately didn't materialise. It's not surprising that he was top in every attacking metric for the game.
It was the sixth straight Premier League game in which he has scored - matching his entire tally from last season - extending what was already the longest scoring streak by any Bournemouth player, or any Brazilian, in the competition.
It is perhaps all the more surprising then than the 27-year-old was left out of Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad over the international break. This game felt like a statement the Italian would be remiss to ignore again.
Charlotte Marsh
Forest's lack of goals could be their downfall
Oliver Glasner called on Nottingham Forest to be ruthless at either end after another Premier League defeat.
For the second time in three league matches, Forest had just one shot on target. In a further three games, just two.

The issue isn't creation. Glasner's team went into this weekend having the fourth-highest number of shots in the league and were just one behind Bournemouth on Saturday for that total (18).
It is the finishing that is their issue - only 37 of their 181 shots this season have been on target - despite having the likes of Liam Delap, Morgan Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus in their team.
Their lowest shot total of the season so far was in their 3-1 win against Man City before the international break (11), perfectly demonstrating how quality wins out over quantity.
Glasner very quickly needs to find whatever happy medium works to get Nottingham Forest turning these shots into not just shots on target, but goals. They are currently above the relegation places on goal difference and everything counts in what is proving to be another tough season at the bottom end of the table.
Charlotte Marsh
Coventry on the rise after worrying start
When a 5-0 thrashing at home to Brighton made it a four-game losing streak at the start of this Premier League season for Coventry, the reality of the difficulty of this level was clear. After 25 years away, it was becoming a painful return.
But a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest before the September international break was a fillip. Since then Frank Lampard's side have shifted the narrative. On Saturday, in the win over Crystal Palace, they showed how.
There was quality, with Taiwo Awoniyi finishing a fine team move and Tatushiro Sakamoto scoring a stunner. But there was also fight - a key attribute Lampard picked out after the game - as Coventry battled to edge this tight, intense game with a late scruffy goal.
That combination has proved a winning formula for the Sky Blues, who have won three of their past four at home and who have seen no side score more than their 12 since the start of October. They're up to 13th and, after a lowly start, on the rise.
Peter Smith
Frank's focus on the defence despite positives in opener
Thomas Frank has been upbeat about his return to the Premier League and even a late own goal and defeat at Coventry in his first game back didn't overly dampen his enthusiasm about his project at Crystal Palace.
Speaking afterwards, Frank was keen to pick out positives in Palace's play - and there were elements to like, including the productive partnership of Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen and the way Palace gained control during the second period.
But they have now conceded 27 goals in their first 11 league games of this season - the most they've let in at this stage since 1927/28. While Coventry's first two goals were impressive, the scrappy winner highlighted where Frank's immediate priority is.
Whether there is a personnel solution or whether he looks to a back three, having used a back-four set up on Saturday, remains to be seen. But he will need to find the answer to get rock-bottom Palace moving up the Premier League.
Peter Smith

מחזור משחקי הפרמייר ליג סיפק מספר תפניות מעניינות. מנצ'סטר סיטי הפגינה יכולת פסיבית ואפרורית בתיקו מול פולהאם, בעוד שפולהאם הפגינה אומץ טקטי וקטעה רצף הפסדים ארוך מולם. מנגד, צ'לסי ספגה תבוסה נוספת לאחר שנכנעה לפיזיות של לידס יונייטד, מה שמפעיל לחץ רב על המאמן צ'אבי אלונסו.

בגזרת הצעירים, טוטנהאם רשמה ניצחון ביתי על איפסוויץ' הודות להופעת בכורה חלומית של בן ה-18 לוקה וויליאמס-בארנט, שכבש והפך לשחקן הצעיר בהיסטוריה של המועדון שכבש בהופעת הבכורה שלו בליגה מאז גארת' בייל. במקביל, אסטון ויליה מתמודדת עם חסרונו המשמעותי של יורי טילמנס במרכז השדה.
